name: 74LVC1G3157GW_125
title: 10 Ω single-pole double-throw analog switch
summary: One SPDT analog switch: a common terminal Z connects to Y0 when the select input S is low and to Y1 when S is high, switching break-before-make. It runs from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, the switch passing signals from GND to VCC with 6 Ω to 7.5 Ω typical ON resistance between VCC = 5 V and 2.7 V. The select input has Schmitt-trigger hysteresis and tolerates 5.5 V whatever the supply, so 3.3 V and 5 V logic can both drive it. Six 6-pin packages share one pinout, rated from -40 °C to +125 °C.

operation.text: S low closes Z to Y0; S high closes Z to Y1. The opened channel lets go before the other closes, at least 0.5 ns apart, at every supply. The switch conducts both ways, so Z and the Y terminals each serve as input or output.

S has Schmitt-trigger hysteresis, so slow edges are accepted up to 20 ns/V below VCC = 2.7 V and 10 ns/V above. It is overvoltage tolerant to 5.5 V at any supply, its thresholds are TTL compatible at VCC = 3.3 V, and it can be driven from 3.3 V or 5 V logic. Holding S at VCC - 0.6 V instead of the rail adds up to 500 µA of supply current at VCC = 5.5 V.

The switched signal runs from 0 V to VCC. Continuous switch current is rated 32 mA, absolute maximum ±50 mA. When current enters a Y terminal and leaves at Z, the drop across the switch must stay at 0.4 V or below to keep current from being drawn out of GND through Z; current entering at Z has no such limit.

From VCC = 1.8 V to 3.3 V, ON resistance has a peak in the upper half of the signal range (near 1 V input at VCC = 1.8 V, near 2.4 V at 3.3 V); at VCC = 5 V it is lowest mid-range, near 2.5 V input. It rises with temperature at all but the 1.8 V supply, where the peak is highest when cold (about 47 Ω at -40 °C against 26 Ω at 125 °C). Typical: 7.5 Ω at VCC = 2.7 V, 6.5 Ω at 3.3 V, 6 Ω at 5 V.
Signal delay through the closed switch is given as typical switch resistance multiplied by load capacitance, for an ideal zero-impedance source.
All six packages carry the code YJ; the pin 1 mark sits at the lower left corner beneath the code.
